messages:
alex_chen: heads-up — we're seeing a sustained TPS surge in dedicated-eu-west-42 causing token-per-second SLO violations. Customers (blueharbor + a few smaller tenants) got 429s starting ~10:02UTC and some downstream 500s from auth proxy. Alert: admission_controller.tps_violation > 90% for 6m. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/INC-2392 :rotating_light:

maria-g: can you paste the pool status and any admission logs? also, did autoscaler kick?

alex_chen: quick dump from the pool endpoint (sanitized):
```
{
  "pool_id": "dedicated-eu-west-42",
  "nodes": 8,
  "pool_capacity": 512,
  "inflight_requests": 640,
  "burst_credit_balance": 0,
  "headroom_slots": 2,
  "admission_mode": "hard",
  "last_refill": "2026-02-15T09:59:58Z",
  "refill_rate_per_sec": 1
}
```

alex_chen: also seeing auth proxy log snippets: 401 on token refresh loop + occasional 502s to model runtime. excerpt:
```
[09:59:59] auth-proxy error: refresh_token failed status=401 reason=expired_key
[10:02:05] gateway warn: upstream=runtime-12 overloaded queue_len=2048 cpu_gpusat=98%
[10:02:12] admission drop: request_id=abc123 reason=burst_credit_exhausted
```

ton y_sre: tagging in. two quick hypotheses: 1) burst credits drained then refill rate was too low for the incoming burst profile, 2) autoscaler failed to scale because prewarm/scale policy uses a 2-min cooldown. can you run the pool health and the billing ledger for credits?

alex_chen: billing shows burst_credit_balance went negative briefly for pool meta-account, but ledger entries look odd. jamie_support, you there? customer complains their dedicated plan should have reserve slots.

jamie_support: on it. customer report: "we spiked to ~750 TPS for ~70s" — they expected us to absorb to 800 for short bursts. I'll ask to temporarily bump their reserved headroom while we triage.

maria-g: repro plan: simulate with k6 with short high concurrency to mimic the spike and capture admission_controller logs + auth proxy. sample k6 snippet to reproduce:
```javascript
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  for (let i=0;i<200;i++) {
    http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', '{"prompt":"ping"}', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <token>'} });
  }
  sleep(0.5);
}
```
run that from 6 workers for 90s to approximate incoming TPS.

tony_sre: also check the operator config: admission_controller.refill_window (defaults to 60s) and burst_credit_decay. if refill_rate_per_sec=1, a 700 TPS spike will drain in <1s. consider temporary config flip: set admission_mode=soft (weighted QoS) and bump headroom_slots to 64 for the pool to avoid hard drops.

alex_chen: tried setting admission_mode=soft via ops-api earlier but autoscale cooldown returned pool to hard mode after 30s. looks like a reconciliation loop from the autoscaler component. opsbot, any automation logs?

opsbot: automation: scheduled_scale_policy_reconcile for pool dedicated-eu-west-42 at 2026-02-15T10:03:15Z. action=ensure_policy state=reconciled (no-op)

maria-g: that reconcile noop suggests the autoscaler thought current node count matched target. need to inspect metric delay: scale decision uses 60s window, but our metric pipeline had ~20s ingestion lag (we saw a prometheus scrape timeout). that explains delayed scale.

jamie_support: immediate mitigation plan: 1) temporary headroom bump to 64 and set admission_mode=soft for the affected pool (tony to execute), 2) notify blueharbor of short-term reserved capacity increase, 3) billing/ledger team to audit burst_credit deductions (jamie -> billing), 4) maria to run repro in staging to confirm fixes.

tony_sre: executing mitigation now. running:
```
# opsctl put-pool-config --pool dedicated-eu-west-42 --set admission_mode=soft --set headroom_slots=64
# opsctl trigger-scale --pool dedicated-eu-west-42 --target-nodes 12 --reason "mitigate TPS surge"
```

alex_chen: after bump, initial metrics show inflight dropped to 420 and 429s subsided. keeping watch. will follow-up with postmortem.

maria-g: postmortem items to capture: metric ingestion lag root cause, autoscaler reconciliation race, refill_rate config default too low for our burst profiles, and authz token rotation handling under load.

jamie_support: customer notified with temporary credit/headroom bump and ETA for postmortem. closing loop in ticket INC-2392 once postmortem linked. :white_check_mark:
